paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend. When the LORD says a word, it stands. He tells Jeremiah that the day has come to destroy the Philistines, and then says, "the LORD is about to destroy the Philistines" (Jeremiah 47:4). Nobody in that passage gets to talk Him out of it, not the allies, not the fathers, not even the sword itself.

That part is heavy, and I think it's supposed to be. Even the cry in the passage, "how long until you rest?", gets this answer: "How can it rest when the LORD has commanded it?" (Jeremiah 47:6-7). Look at what that tells us. The sword doesn't move on its own, and it doesn't stop on its own. Everything in this word answers to the LORD, and nobody else is running the show. Tyre and Sidon couldn't help, and that includes the next ally you're tempted to lean on.

So here's what I'm taking to the oven, baker. God's word is not a suggestion. It's not a rumor, and it's not a maybe. When He speaks, you can build your whole day on it. That's why I keep my ovens ready, and it's why I want you in this Word, where you can hear Him for yourself.
